_comment: Fires BEFORE the OOM kill. That is the entire value - alerting on an OOMKill that already happened tells you about an outage you did not prevent.

documentation.content:
A CONTAINER IS NEAR ITS MEMORY LIMIT. AN OOMKILL IS COMING.

Memory is INCOMPRESSIBLE. Unlike CPU, which throttles, exceeding the memory limit means the kernel kills the container instantly (exit 137) with no chance to log anything.

First command:
  kubectl top pods -n orders

Decide which of two very different situations this is:

  LIMIT TOO LOW - memory rises then plateaus (sawtooth). The app legitimately
                  needs more. Raise the limit.
  MEMORY LEAK   - memory climbs monotonically and never returns. Raising the
                  limit only delays the crash. Fix the leak.

The shape of the memory graph over an hour distinguishes them.

Fix (limit too low):
  helm upgrade orders-api ./helm/application ... --set resources.limits.memory=256Mi

Also check whether it is NODE memory pressure rather than the container limit:
  kubectl describe node | grep MemoryPressure
